Plays out the exchange in order of counting value and says who comes out ahead
Finds the winning capture sequence in a mixed position

steps.text:
This lesson follows **X-ray and batteries: the piece behind joins in**. There you were told that an x-ray existed. Now you count it yourself.
On the square in question list your attackers, including each piece standing behind another on the same line, and then the defenders. Play the exchange with the cheapest piece first. Either side may stop, so ask who runs out of pieces first.

**The count works** when the rear piece stands on the same line and the front piece will leave by capture or by moving. **It fails** when the front piece cannot capture, or when a second defender arrives. **Rule of thumb:** counting values 1, 3, 3, 5, 9 only guide the order; check the last capture, because the side that makes it must not be recaptured.

steps.title: Same exchange, one change
steps.prompt: White to move: does the first rook capture on the e-file win a rook? One change each time. Predict, then check.
Pick one silent position. Write the attackers of the key square, including the pieces behind, then the defenders, then who runs out first. Was your first count right?

steps.text: **Remember.** On the key square, list your attackers, including each piece standing behind another on the same line, then the defenders. Play the exchange with the cheapest piece first and ask who runs out first. It fails if the front piece cannot capture or a second defender arrives. Check the last capture: it must not be recaptured.
